steps.comment: SpeedLM: a vLLM server that retrains its own speculative decoder while idle.
this is how you serve Qwen3-8B on plain vLLM.
this is SpeedLM. same server, same model, one added flag.
last run trained 8 epochs. the gate liked the quality and still refused it.
verdict said promote. stationarity vetoed it, and the run rolled itself back.
8 epochs drove val accuracy to 0.988 -- and on-policy acceptance DOWN to 0.549.
that is memorising the window, not learning the traffic. so: scale data, not epochs.
this run moves exactly one knob. everything else is held fixed.
one epoch. that flag is running right now, as SLURM job 380545.
it is seeded with real agentic-coding traffic -- nothing synthetic.
the traffic stopped. the tuner noticed, slept vLLM, and took the GPU.
it rendered training rows out of a 1024-record window and started fitting.
every loss below is being written by the trainer, live, as you watch it.
steps.command: timeout 7200 tail --pid=$(pgrep -f speculators/scripts/train.py | head -1) -F -n +1 "$L" 2>/dev/null | grep --line-buffered -oE 'epoch [0-9]+/[0-9]+ started|train/loss=[0-9.]+|val/loss_epoch=[0-9.]+, epoch=[0-9]+'

steps.comment: one pass over the data. now the gate -- is it faster, and does it still agree?
steps.command: timeout 5400 tail -F -n +1 $H/runs/events.jsonl | jq --unbuffered -r '"\(.from) -> \(.to)   \(.reason)"' | stdbuf -oL awk '{print substr($0,1,96)} /-> READY/&&NR>1{exit}'

steps.comment: and the numbers the gate decided on -- measured, not claimed.
quality is only half of it -- the speed number also has to hold still to count.
per-repeat, the raw tok/s the verdict was computed from:
one flag, one epoch. the server tuned itself, measured itself, and judged itself.
